name: Phoenix
description: A long-lived bird of classical mythology that, at the end of its life, builds a nest, ignites, and is reborn from its own ashes. Frequently identified by ancient writers with the Egyptian Bennu and adopted across Roman, Christian, alchemical, and modern symbolism as an emblem of renewal.

aliases.name: φοῖνιξ (phoinix)
aliases.meaning: phoenix; possibly derived from a West Semitic word for the red dye 'madder'

aliases.name: Bennu
aliases.meaning: Egyptian solar bird associated with creation and rebirth, often identified by classical authors with the Greek phoenix

aliases.name: Fenghuang
aliases.meaning: Chinese 'phoenix' — a separate mythological bird often translated using the same English word

aliases.name: Huma
aliases.meaning: Persian mythological bird sometimes compared to the phoenix

aliases.name: Anqa / Simurgh
aliases.meaning: Other related Near Eastern mythological birds

origin: Mythological — described in classical literature as native to Arabia, Egypt, Ethiopia, or India, depending on the author. The phoenix has no real geographic range.
